programs.name: Lasting Adventures - Yosemite
programs.description: Introductory 6-day wilderness backpacking camp in Yosemite for ages 11-13.

flags.title: No parent contact during the trip
flags.body: Guides send a nightly satellite check-in to the office, not to families. Parents should expect zero direct communication with their child for the length of the trip barring an actual emergency.
flags.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures Yosemite summer camp FAQ

dayToDay.notes: Students are with their guide group essentially the entire trip, sleeping outdoors at shared backcountry campsites, with a staff-to-camper ratio of at least 2 staff per 10 youth. Days are highly structured: hiking, a daily morning meeting, evening group activities and a campfire, and shared meals prepared together. There's no cell service in the backcountry, so there's no phone or text contact with family during the trip — guides send a nightly satellite check-in to the office, not to parents, consistent with the program's "no news is good news" approach. Parents receive a recap email with photos and a daily journal about 1–2 weeks after the trip ends.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures Yosemite summer camp FAQ pages (identical language across 6-Day Young Adventurer's, 6-Day High Country, and 10-Day Mammoth pages)

programs.name: Catalina Sea Camp
programs.description: One-week ocean adventure and marine science overnight camp on Catalina Island for ages 8-13.

dayToDay.notes: This is an island-based residential camp with structured cabin groups of about 8-10 campers per counselor; certified dive staff supervise at closer ratios (1 instructor per 4 campers for scuba certification, 1 per 8 for snorkeling). There is no phone contact between parents and campers at all during a session - the camp states this is an intentional independence policy, not just a logistics limitation. The only outbound communication is one-way: parents get 5 free email credits per camper per week (more purchasable), and campers can write letters, but there's no video call or phone option. In-session visits or tours from parents are not permitted. A registered nurse is on-site for the full summer.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Catalina Sea Camp 1-Week Programs page and Parent FAQs

programs.name: Honors Summer Math Camp (HSMC)
programs.description: Intensive six-week residential math camp at Texas State University; first-year students take a discovery-style number theory course, returning multi-summer students move into original research projects.
programs.gradeDisplay: Grades 9-11, first-year admission concentrated in current 9th-10th graders

flags.title: No online courses or other programs allowed during camp
flags.body: HSMC explicitly prohibits campers from taking any online courses or participating in any other program - in person or virtual - for the full six weeks. Families should not plan for a student to double up on summer commitments.
flags.sourceCitation: Mathworks HSMC program page

dayToDay.notes: This is a highly structured, academically intensive residential program: the daily schedule runs from 7am breakfast to 10pm, with classes and research in the morning, problem sessions or additional classes in the afternoon, and study groups in the evening. Campers are explicitly not permitted to take online courses or participate in any other program, in person or online, during the six weeks. Parent visits during camp are allowed but require prior approval through a request form, rather than being either fully open or fully prohibited.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Mathworks HSMC program page and Camps visit-request page (txst.edu/mathworks)

programs.name: Junior Summer Math Camp - Residential (JSMCR)
programs.description: Two-week residential math camp at Texas State University for middle schoolers, combining daily math classes with study groups, recreation, and camp outings.

flags.title: No online courses or other programs allowed during camp
flags.body: Unlike most residential summer programs, JSMCR explicitly prohibits campers from taking any online courses or participating in any other program - in person or virtual - for the full two weeks. Families should not plan for a student to double up on summer commitments.
flags.sourceCitation: Mathworks JSMCR program page

dayToDay.notes: Students live in a campus dormitory supervised by camp counselors at a ratio of 1 counselor to 4 students - closer supervision than the HSMC high schooler program. Days include daily math classes taught by university professors, study group sessions, and recreation time with free use of the university's Student Recreation Center (basketball, volleyball, racquetball, indoor track, pool). Fridays include a guest lecture from an academic or industry speaker followed by a picnic with games at a local park. As with HSMC, campers are not permitted to take online courses or participate in any other program during the two weeks.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Mathworks JSMCR program page and JSMCR Daily Schedule and Events page (txst.edu/mathworks)

programs.name: NYC Summer Academy
programs.institution: The School of The New York Times
programs.description: Two-week journalism and media pre-college program in NYC taught by NYT journalists and industry experts; day students commute daily.
programs.gradeDisplay: Rising grades 10-12 and graduating seniors, ages 15-18
programs.datesDisplay: Four 2-week terms, June-July 2027 (exact per-term dates not available - site blocks direct fetch)

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live in a dorm-style facility in Manhattan, with roommates assigned by gender identity and age. Building security and residential staff are present in the residence hall 24/7, and Residential Directors live adjacent to the students they oversee. Both residential and day students participate in a structured set of evening and weekend activities beyond the academic day. Day students commute in for the academic portion and have the option to stay for dinner and evening/weekend programming, but go home (or to their own housing) at night rather than living on-site.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: NYT Edu 'Program Experience' and NYC Summer Academy pages

programs.name: Junior Summer Math Camp - Half-Day (JSMCH)
programs.description: Two-week, non-residential half-day math enrichment camp in San Marcos for grades 3-8; students explore algebra and problem-solving through hands-on activities.
programs.datesDisplay: 2027 dates not yet published on the official program page
programs.priceDisplay: Contact program — listed at $400 for the 2026 session on site

dayToDay.notes: This is a day program with no overnight component - parents drop off and pick up daily, and San Marcos CISD provides bus transportation, but only for students enrolled in that local school district (families outside the district must arrange their own transportation, as Mathworks itself doesn't provide any). Breakfast, lunch, and a snack are provided during the school day. Students are on campus only during camp hours and go home each evening.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Mathworks JSMCH program page (txst.edu/mathworks)

programs.name: Management & Technology Summer Institute (M&TSI)
programs.description: Highly selective 3-week residential program at Wharton and Penn Engineering combining business and technology coursework, culminating in a student-built tech venture prototype; earns 1 Penn college credit.
programs.gradeDisplay: Rising seniors (some rising juniors admitted per third-party sources)

flags.title: No partial attendance or early departure permitted
flags.body: Students must attend from the first day to the last day of the three-week program with no exceptions - the program explicitly states this is required because college credit is awarded for the full session. Families with a conflicting commitment (e.g., another camp, a family trip) cannot plan around a partial stay.
flags.sourceCitation: M&TSI FAQs page

flags.title: The $12,000 fee doesn't cover the following:
flags.body: Not included in the program fee: the $100 non-refundable application fee, travel to/from Philadelphia, Pottruck Gym access, off-campus meals (including all Saturdays, when no meals are provided at all), medical expenses, laundry, and personal spending money.
flags.sourceCitation: M&TSI program page, fee breakdown

dayToDay.notes: Students live in Penn dormitories with a meal plan in the undergraduate dining halls, described by the program as including 'student supervision.' The schedule is described as extremely rigorous and non-stop given that a full college credit is earned in just three weeks. Meals are provided twice daily Monday-Friday and twice on Sunday, but there are no provided meals at all on Saturdays, which are reserved for excursions and off-campus activities - students should budget for that. Full attendance is mandatory from the first day to the last; the program does not permit partial attendance or early departure under any circumstances, since credit is tied to completing the full three weeks.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: M&TSI program page and FAQs (fisher.wharton.upenn.edu)

programs.name: Oxford Academia at Yale
programs.description: Two-week residential Ivy League immersion program at Yale where students choose a major and minor seminar from subjects spanning business, law, medicine, AI, and the humanities.
programs.gradeDisplay: Completing grades 9-12 (motivated rising 9th graders also considered)
programs.priceDisplay: Contact program — tuition not yet published on site

flags.title: Org's own pages disagree on whether tuition covers 3 meals a day
flags.body: The general Oxford Academia FAQ page states Yale tuition 'includes all accommodations and three meals each day,' but the Yale-specific program page states lunches are not included in tuition and are handled independently by students. Families should confirm directly which is accurate before budgeting.
flags.sourceCitation: Oxford Academia FAQ page vs. Yale program page (both oxfordacademia.com)

flags.title: Tuition (once published) will exclude several real costs
flags.body: Per the general FAQ: the $200 non-refundable application fee, airfare/travel to the program, lunches, classroom/art supplies, laundry, communication home, health care, and personal expenses are all separate from tuition. Airport group transportation to campus (JFK or Bradley) costs $65 each way if used.
flags.sourceCitation: Oxford Academia FAQ page

dayToDay.notes: Students live in double suite-style dorm rooms with bathrooms on the hall, with faculty and residential staff (Deans, Student Deans, Junior Deans, and Health & Activity Coordinators) living in the same residence halls, focused specifically on student life and well-being. The academic day is structured: major seminar meets six days a week for three hours, minor seminar meets three days a week for two hours, with afternoons/evenings open for electives and extracurriculars, and evening programming (guest speakers, shows, or college-admissions Q&As) bringing all seminar groups together after dinner. Breakfasts and dinners are provided at the dorm cafeteria, but lunches are not included in tuition - students handle lunch independently in small peer groups, a mix of city restaurants and picnics. On weekends, students go on staff-led or seminar-group excursions, which may include a day trip to New York City.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Oxford Academia at Yale program page (oxfordacademia.com)

programs.name: SOCAPA - New York City
programs.institution: School of Creative and Performing Arts (SOCAPA)
programs.description: Two-week pre-college screenwriting and filmmaking intensive in Manhattan; day format.
programs.gradeDisplay: Ages 14-18 (grade range converted from published ages)

flags.title: Meals are not included in the Manhattan residential fee
flags.body: Unlike SOCAPA's Los Angeles and Vermont campuses, where room & board includes three daily meals Mon-Fri, Manhattan residential students must purchase their own meals for the entire session (with brief counselor guidance the first three days only). Families should budget separately for food.
flags.sourceCitation: SOCAPA Tuition & Costs page

dayToDay.notes: Day students attend roughly 9:45am-4pm; residential students live in NYU-area dormitory housing with lounges, computer rooms, and laundry facilities, with staff living in residence. Uniquely among SOCAPA's campuses, meals are NOT included in the Manhattan residential fee - students are responsible for purchasing their own food. For the first three days, counselors guide students to nearby restaurants and delis in Greenwich Village/East Village; after that, students sign out and explore food options in self-organized small groups (never alone, per policy). Every weekday evening (Monday-Friday) a planned activity is scheduled - a campus barbecue, a dinner out in the city, a pool visit, a theater or musical performance, or a film screening. Saturday afternoons not spent shooting/rehearsing are reserved for a group excursion (past examples include Coney Island, Broadway shows, and various museums), and at least once per session SOCAPA brings in an industry professional (actors, writers, directors) to lead a master class open to all students regardless of track. Unlike other SOCAPA campuses, there is no unaccompanied-minor airport pickup/drop-off service offered at all at the NYC campus.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: SOCAPA NYC campus page and SOCAPA Tuition & Costs page (socapa.org)

programs.name: Westcoast Connection - Pre-College Enrichment (UCLA)
programs.description: Pre-college enrichment program on the UCLA campus; students choose one morning and one afternoon course from a wide catalog (business, law, psychology, science, arts, languages); residential format.

flags.title: Lunch is not included in tuition, despite meals being advertised as covered
flags.body: Program pages list breakfast and dinner as included, but lunch is explicitly excluded and paid for independently by students each day - worth budgeting for separately.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA program pages, 'What's Included' section

flags.title: Advertised price includes a limited-time discount
flags.body: The prices shown ($6,399 for 14 days, $8,599 for 21 days, $11,499 for 27 days with Hawaii) reflect active 'enroll early and save' promotions off list prices of $6,699, $8,999, and $11,999 respectively. The discount is time-limited and not guaranteed to still apply later in the enrollment cycle.
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA program pages (14-, 21-, and 27-day)

flags.title: Not a UCLA-run program despite the branding
flags.body: The program page includes an explicit disclaimer: this is operated by Westcoast Connection, not UCLA. Students stay in UCLA housing and use UCLA facilities, and some instructors are UCLA Extension faculty, but 'responsibility for the program resides solely with Westcoast Connection.'
flags.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA 14-day, 21-day, and 27-day program pages

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live in suite-style housing at Delta Terrace in Sunset Village, with their own bathroom, and staff (residence life coordinators among them) living in the same halls. A typical day: 8am wake-up, 8:30 breakfast, 9:30-11:30 morning course, 11:30 lunch (unstructured - students choose where to eat in small groups, on or off campus), 1:30-3:30 afternoon course, then free time until 6pm dinner, followed by organized evening activities. Breakfast and dinner are included in tuition; lunch is explicitly NOT included and is handled independently by students. Commuter (day) students attend roughly 9:30am-3:30/4pm on class days only, are not housed overnight, have no meals included, get limited access to UCLA recreational facilities, and may optionally join group field trips or the college-admissions workshops.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA 14-day and 21-day program pages (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live at Residence La Citadelle, McGill University, in individual twin-bed rooms with private bathrooms, air conditioning, housekeeping service, and a personal work desk. A typical day: 8am wake-up, 8:30 breakfast, 10am morning course (or start of a full-day track option), lunch break (unstructured - students choose where to eat in small groups), 2pm afternoon course, then free time ('Student's Choice') until 7pm dinner, followed by evening activities until around 9pm. Breakfast and dinner are included in tuition; lunch is not and is handled independently by students. Commuter (day) students attend roughly 10am-4/4:30pm on class days only, are not housed overnight, have no meals included, get limited access to McGill's recreational facilities, and may optionally join the college-admissions workshops.

programs.name: MIT Women's Technology Program (WTP)
programs.description: Highly selective four-week residential engineering program at MIT for young women and other underrepresented/underserved students in engineering; hands-on classes, labs, and team projects in mechanical engineering, taught by MIT graduate students with undergraduate assistants living in the dorm. No prior engineering background expected or desired.
programs.gradeDisplay: Current 11th graders only (not rising seniors generally - must be in 11th grade at time of application)
programs.priceDisplay: Sliding scale by family income: free for family AGI ≤$120,000; $2,000 ($120-150K); $4,000 ($150-200K); $8,000 ($200-400K); $20,000 (≥$400K); further aid available if these amounts are a hardship

flags.title: Eligibility depends on family home address, not school location
flags.body: A student's eligibility is based on where their family's permanent home address is (must be in the US year-round), not where they attend school. This means a student at a US boarding school with a family home abroad is ineligible, while a student at a boarding school abroad with a US family home is eligible.
flags.sourceCitation: MIT WTP FAQ page

dayToDay.notes: Students live in an MIT dorm alongside the MIT undergraduate students who serve as teaching assistants. Daily required classes run Monday-Friday from approximately 9:30am-5pm, with occasional evening hours, plus some planned weekend academic field trips and social outings. The schedule includes classes, labs, homework, and unstructured social time with other WTP students. Students are expected to have no other significant time commitments during the four weeks. A laptop is expected for coursework; free loaners are available for students who need one.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: MIT WTP calendar and FAQ pages (wtp.mit.edu)

flags.body: Interlochen has faced historical abuse allegations, underwent an external investigation, and received donations from Jeffrey Epstein from 1990 to 2003. Review recent safety reporting and institutional responses before enrolling.

flags.title: One-week Intensives are not eligible for financial aid

dayToDay.notes: Students live in one of over 120 cabins across Interlochen's 1,200-acre campus, organized by division. Days combine classes, rehearsals, and coursework with time for swimming in one of two campus lakes, crafts, pickup sports, and other traditional camp activities. Programs longer than one week that require an audition or portfolio are automatically considered for merit scholarships; need-based financial aid is also available for any program longer than one week (one-week Intensives are not aid-eligible). Admission for all programs is submitted through Interlochen's Education Community portal, with a Jan. 15 priority deadline for the following summer.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Interlochen Arts Camp tuition/financial aid page and general camp materials (interlochen.org)

dayToDay.notes: Students live in one of over 120 cabins across Interlochen's 1,200-acre campus, grouped with other Intermediate-age campers. Alongside daily rehearsals/coursework in their chosen program, students have time for traditional camp activities - swimming, field games, and archery. Every program at this division runs 3 or 6 weeks and is eligible for need-based financial aid; programs longer than one week that require an audition or portfolio are automatically considered for merit scholarships. Admission is submitted through Interlochen's Education Community portal, with a Jan. 15 priority deadline for the following summer.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Interlochen grades 6-8 program pages and tuition/financial aid page (interlochen.org)

programs.name: EXPLO Middle School
programs.description: Broad custom-curriculum track: students choose 2 workshops and 2 electives from 50+ options. Dates confirmed directly via EXPLO's 2027 registration form.
programs.priceDisplay: $6,295 (2026 reference figure; 2027 price not yet published)

flags.title: Focus Programs (Veterinary Science, Medical Rotations) exclude rising 7th graders
flags.body: Unlike EXPLO 360, which is open to the full rising 7-9 grade band, both Focus Programs are restricted to rising 8th and 9th graders only. A rising 7th grader can only enroll in EXPLO 360.
flags.sourceCitation: EXPLO 2027 registration form

flags.title: "4 weeks" is not a distinct product - it's enrolling in both sessions
flags.body: The registration form only lists 2-week Session 1 and Session 2 options; a family wanting the full 4 weeks selects Session 1, completes payment, then is prompted to separately select Session 2. A Double Session Discount applies ($500 overnight/$300 day per the 2026 schedule) but there is no single bundled '4-week' product.
flags.sourceCitation: EXPLO 2027 registration form instructions

flags.title: Extra fee for unaccompanied-minor airport service, and a caution against flying that way
flags.body: EXPLO explicitly recommends students NOT fly as unaccompanied minors unless required by the airline, and charges an extra $150 each way if a family does use EXPLO's transportation for an unaccompanied minor.
flags.sourceCitation: EXPLO Tuition + Financial Aid page

dayToDay.notes: EXPLO is explicitly an 'unplugged' program - device use is restricted as a stated program value, not merely a default policy. Residential students live in Wellesley College dorms with roommates, supported by Resident Advisors around the clock; a general staff-to-student ratio of 1:7 is advertised. Weekends are student-choice: options include whale watching, Red Sox games, museum visits, and other off-campus trips, with a 24/7 health center on site. Day students follow the same academic day as residential students but go home at night; if a day student stays for evening programming, a $38 dinner + evening event fee is charged to their account. International students live alongside domestic students in the same dorms and dining halls.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: EXPLO program details and tuition/FAQ pages (explo.org)

flags.sourceCitation: EXPLO Tuition + Financial Aid page

flags.title: Pre-med / health careers focus track
flags.body: Medical Rotations is EXPLO Middle School's pre-med oriented Focus Program: a fixed curriculum shadowing medical fields rather than the custom EXPLO 360 workshop menu. Rising 8th and 9th graders only.
flags.sourceCitation: EXPLO 2027 registration form (explo.org)

dayToDay.notes: EXPLO is explicitly an 'unplugged' program - device use is restricted as a stated program value, not merely a default policy. Residential students live in Wellesley College dorms with roommates, supported by Resident Advisors around the clock; a general staff-to-student ratio of 1:7 is advertised. Weekends are student-choice: options include whale watching, Red Sox games, museum visits, and other off-campus trips, with a 24/7 health center on site. Day students follow the same academic day as residential students but go home at night; if a day student stays for evening programming, a $38 dinner + evening event fee is charged to their account. International students live alongside domestic students in the same dorms and dining halls.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: EXPLO program details and tuition/FAQ pages (explo.org)

programs.creditDisplay: Optional 4 college credits via CIEE partner
programs.priceDisplay: $7,300 + $25 application fee (+ optional $250 college credit fee)

dayToDay.notes: Students live with a host family (homestay) in Shanghai for the duration of the program, preparing and sharing Chinese meals together as part of daily language and cultural immersion. Three meals a day are provided overall with dietary needs accommodated, and all ground transportation once in-country, all cultural activities and excursions, and interactive language classes are included. Wi-Fi access is available at accommodations, but no international data plan or SIM card is included. Pre-departure advice and orientation are provided before travel, and CIEE provides 24/7 emergency on-site support plus comprehensive medical and travel protection (iNext Travel Insurance) throughout the program. An optional flight chaperone is available (flight cost itself is not included in tuition).

programs.name: CIEE - Honors Spanish Language & Culture (Madrid)
programs.description: Intensive, Spanish-only immersion program (a Language Pledge covering in- and out-of-class time) for intermediate/advanced speakers, gated by a pre-program STAMP proficiency test and completed high school Spanish Level 2+ with a minimum ACTFL Intermediate-Low score. Homestay-based; activities/excursions are with other Honors students only, including a trip to Valencia. CIEE has not published Session I dates for 2027 as of this research pass.

flags.title: Requires a pre-program Spanish proficiency test
flags.body: This Honors program is gated by a pre-program STAMP language proficiency test. Students must have completed high school Spanish Level 2 or higher and score at least Intermediate-Low on the ACTFL scale; those who do not meet the bar may be moved to a standard (non-Honors) Language & Culture program instead. Students who don't yet meet the criteria are directed to apply to the standard programs in Barcelona, Madrid, Palma, Seville, Buenos Aires, or Merida as a second choice.

dayToDay.notes: Students travel as a single group of 12 with 3 adult leaders throughout the trip, camping in the backcountry (San Juan National Forest) for the backpacking segment and along the riverbank during the 2-day whitewater rafting section, with no fixed base camp. As with all Moondance trips, the program is explicitly 'unplugged' - phones and social media use are restricted as a stated program value - and there is no routine parent contact during the trip itself.

programs.name: Broadreach - 7-Day Scuba + Sailing Expedition
programs.description: Entry-level liveaboard week combining scuba and sailing; PADI Scuba Diver or Advanced Open Water certification plus one sailing certification available. No experience required.

dayToDay.notes: Students live aboard a sailing vessel for the entire program, sharing cabins with a small crew of peers and instructors. Days are structured around the boat's itinerary - sailing between islands, scuba instruction and dives, and shore stops for excursions - with instructors present around the clock in the shared living space. There is no fixed land base; the boat itself is the accommodation throughout.

programs.name: ARCC - Belize
programs.description: Marine biology and coral reef conservation program on a private Caribbean island; includes PADI Open Water or Advanced Open Water SCUBA certification, lionfish removal, and a visit to Xunantunich Mayan ruins. Only one departure offered.
programs.priceDisplay: $6,488 (airfare for group flight from Houston additional)

dayToDay.notes: Students stay primarily on a private Caribbean island for the SCUBA portion of the trip, with some time on the mainland for cultural excursions. Transportation includes shuttles, vans, and a private boat to the island. Showers are available most days; there is no machine laundry, so handwashing/air-drying is expected. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Belize program page (arccprograms.com)

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation varies across the trip: hotels, rustic camping shelters, a jungle lodge, and dorm-style bungalows. Transportation is by private bus/van arranged by ARCC's in-country partner. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders.

programs.name: ARCC - Spain and Morocco
programs.description: Spanish language lessons, flamenco and cooking classes in Southern Spain, followed by a homestay-style cultural exchange with an Amazigh community in Morocco's High Atlas Mountains. Only one departure offered.
programs.priceDisplay: $7,388 (airfare for group flight from New York additional)

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation varies: Moroccan riads, local Spanish homes, hotels, and an Amazigh community guesthouse in the High Atlas Mountains. Travel includes private shuttles, vans, trains, and a ferry crossing of the Strait of Gibraltar. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Spain & Morocco program page

programs.name: ARCC - Peru
programs.description: Cultural immersion in the Sacred Valley including Machu Picchu, Rainbow Mountain, and llama herding with Quechua communities. Explicitly has no community service component, unlike most other ARCC programs. Only one departure offered.
programs.priceDisplay: $5,388 (airfare for group flight from Miami additional)

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation varies: simple hotels, hostels, homestays, and a village community house. Travel is by train and private bus. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders. High altitude (Cusco is over 11,000 feet) - the itinerary builds in acclimatization time.

programs.name: Summer Discovery - UCLA Middle School
programs.description: UCLA is the only Summer Discovery campus offering both a standard Middle School track AND an Institute for the Gifted track at the same grade band (6-8) - both price identically and are combined here. Available topics: Young Entrepreneurs (NFTE), Marketing & Advertising, Robotics Masterminds, Data Detectives, AI Pioneers, Crack the Code (cryptography), Creative Writing, Film Production, Fashion Design, Money Matters (finance), Biomedical Engineering Design Lab, Hit the Gavel (Mock Trial/Debate), Speak with Confidence (Rhetoric & Debate), Mock Trial, Forensic Investigation, Microbe Detectives, Foundations of Psychology, Wormholes & Time Warps (physics), Discrete Math, Sports Leadership with IMG Academy.

dayToDay.notes: At UCLA, High School students have an exclusive residence hall not shared with any other program (Hedrick Summit), fully air-conditioned. Tuition includes academic instruction, housing, 2 meals/day (lunch and dinner), and extracurricular activities/excursions every afternoon, evening, and weekend, plus use of athletic/recreation facilities. programs.name: Overland - Alaska Explorer
programs.description: Alaska wilderness trip for the Explorer tier (grades 6-9 band).

dayToDay.notes: Overland is explicitly screen-free as a stated program value, and is accredited by the American Camp Association. Groups are small (typically capped at 10-12 students) and are usually a mix of two adjacent grades. Meals are prepared as group projects rather than served to students. Students fly into a specific gateway city/airport per trip, where Overland leaders provide supervised arrival and departure - the exact city varies by trip (e.g., Anchorage for Alaska trips, Zurich for Alpine Challenge, Bozeman for Montana trips). Camping style varies by trip - primarily frontcountry (with facilities) for some, extended backcountry/backpacking for others - detailed on each trip's own page. Overland has run since 1984.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Overland Summers trip pages, FAQ, and general marketing pages (overlandsummers.com)

dayToDay.notes: Overland is explicitly screen-free as a stated program value, and is accredited by the American Camp Association. Groups are small (typically capped at 10-12 students) and are usually a mix of two adjacent grades. Meals are prepared as group projects rather than served to students. Students fly into a specific gateway city/airport per trip, where Overland leaders provide supervised arrival and departure - the exact city varies by trip (e.g., Anchorage for Alaska trips, Zurich for Alpine Challenge, Bozeman for Montana trips). Camping style varies by trip - primarily frontcountry (with facilities) for some, extended backcountry/backpacking for others - detailed on each trip's own page. Overland has run since 1984.

programs.name: TFT - Costa Rica Animal Rescue Service
programs.description: Community service at an animal rescue/rehabilitation center, plus adventure activities.

dayToDay.notes: TFT does not publish specific accommodation names for safety reasons (families get this after registering, via a secure parent portal) - generally small, centrally located, family-run hotels rather than large chain hotels. Tuition includes ground transportation, accommodation, chaperones/guides, program activities, taxes/tips, and all meals; airfare, visas, and personal expenses are not included, though an optional group flight is typically offered. programs.description: Overnight whitewater rafting on the Pacuare River (rated among the world's top rivers for rafting) plus community service, tailored for first-time middle school travelers.

dayToDay.notes: First night at a mountain lodge overlooking a volcano in Turrialba, followed by an overnight whitewater rafting trip on the Pacuare River with a night spent in a rainforest lodge along the riverbank. Community service work (~20 hours) takes place alongside adventure activities. Designed specifically to be a gentle first international trip for younger travelers.

programs.locationDisplay: Sunshine Coast, Noosa, Booloumba Creek, Brisbane & Moreton Island

programs.description: A science-course program (the only one of Rustic's 3 Italy programs that is a research course rather than a cultural tour): a five-day taught marine research course with the Delfini del Ponente research group on the Ligurian coast, including bottlenose dolphin photo-identification for a live research catalogue, Posidonia oceanica seagrass snorkel surveys, sunrise sea-turtle-track beach monitoring, and a full day at sea in the Pelagos Sanctuary. Snorkeling is close to shore, weather-dependent, and called off rather than pushed when conditions are wrong. Median staff ratio 4.37:1 org-wide (never exceeding 7:1), max 16 students. programs.name: Rustic Pathways - Ireland & Iceland: Ecovillage to Glacier
programs.description: Rustic Pathways' first student travel program in Ireland: five nights living inside an intentional ecovillage community in Cloughjordan (land care, seed saving, a village fabrication/repair lab), two days on Dublin's circular economy including the Rediscovery Centre, then five days in Iceland examining geothermal power on the Reykjanes Peninsula, hydropower in South Iceland, and a glacier visit. Max 16 students. Ireland is not in the Schengen Area, so the EU's ETIAS authorization does not apply here (unlike most other Rustic Europe programs).

programs.priceDisplay: $6,350 at checkout ($6,250 tuition + $100 enrollment fee) + airfare

Cloughjordan is a rural village with mobile coverage and Wi-Fi but noticeably slower speeds than a city; Dublin connectivity is unrestricted. Median staff ratio 4.37:1 org-wide (never exceeding 7:1), max 16 students, capped separately per departure. programs.name: Rustic Pathways - K-Everything (Spring Break 2027, South Korea)
programs.description: The ONLY non-summer program in the entire Rustic Pathways portfolio researched -- a Spring Break 2027 trip built around K-pop, K-beauty, Korean street food and fashion across Hongdae, Gangnam, Myeongdong, and Seongsu, plus a hanbok experience at Gyeongbokgung Palace and Bukchon Hanok Village. No group or chaperoned flight is offered on this program; families book independently within a narrow overnight-flight arrival/departure window (the page notes the 'U.S. dates' April 4-9 don't match the 'Korea dates' Apr 5-9 due to the international date line and 13-hour time difference -- worth flagging so families don't miscount the days on the ground). Max 14 students. Timed to match Palo Alto Unified and Atlanta Public Schools spring break.
programs.priceDisplay: $1,999 + $100 enrollment fee (estimated) + airfare (no group/chaperoned flight offered)

flags.title: This is the only non-summer program in the portfolio researched
flags.body: This program runs during Spring Break 2027 (April 4-9), not summer. Families used to summer program timelines should note this is a different booking season entirely, timed to match Palo Alto Unified and Atlanta Public Schools spring break.
flags.sourceCitation: South Korea Teen Travel Program: K-Everything program page, Why This Destination? section

flags.title: US travel dates and Korea travel dates are not the same days
flags.body: This program is sold as 'Sunday April 4 to Friday April 9, 2027' using US departure/return dates, but because of the international date line and a 13-hour time difference, students are actually on the ground in Korea only from Monday morning to Friday evening (5 days, 4 nights). Families should not assume 6 full days in Korea based on the marketed date range.
flags.sourceCitation: South Korea Teen Travel Program: K-Everything program page, Flight Times section

flags.title: No group or chaperoned flight is offered
flags.body: Unlike most other Rustic Pathways programs, there is no group flight and no chaperoned flight option here. Every family must book independent international airfare landing at Incheon between 4:00-9:00 AM on the Monday and departing between 6:00-10:00 PM on the Friday, Korea time. Arrivals outside this window incur an additional out-of-window fee.
flags.sourceCitation: South Korea Teen Travel Program: K-Everything program page, Flights & Cost FAQ section

dayToDay.notes: Students room together in gender-separated rooms in a guest house in Seoul, with shared bathrooms, Wi-Fi, and communal spaces. Rustic Pathways Program Leaders stay on-site throughout for 24/7 supervision. Group capped at 14 students. Unlike most Rustic Pathways programs, there is no group or chaperoned flight option here; every family books independently within a strict overnight-flight arrival/departure window (land Incheon 4-9am Monday, depart Incheon 6-10pm Friday, Korea time).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: South Korea Teen Travel Program: K-Everything program page, Accommodation and Flights & Cost FAQ sections

programs.name: Rustic Pathways - Italy & Greece: Culture, Food & Exploration
programs.description: A six-days-per-country split, joined by food: a Venetian mask-making workshop, Lake Garda's Lazise, an Italian cooking class on the coast at Jesolo, and Verona's Roman Arena, then a flight to Athens for the Acropolis, a Peloponnese day (Corinth Canal, Nafplio, Mycenae), Delphi and the mountain village of Arachova, and a final Athens day of markets, street art, a Greek cooking class and dance lesson. Max 20 students; the Italy-to-Athens flight is included in tuition.
programs.locationDisplay: Venice, Lake Garda, Jesolo & Verona, Italy; Athens & the Peloponnese, Greece
programs.priceDisplay: $5,495 at checkout ($5,395 tuition + $100 enrollment fee) + airfare

dayToDay.notes: 2-4 students room together in gender-separated rooms throughout. In Italy, students stay in one base property in the Venice/Lake Garda region with shared common spaces and outdoor areas. In Greece, students stay in a central hotel in Athens for the second half of the program. Program staff stay in adjacent rooms throughout. Median staff ratio 4.37:1 org-wide (never exceeding 7:1), max 20 students (sessions average around 15).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Italy & Greece: Culture, Food & Exploration program page, Accommodation and Group & Logistics FAQ sections

programs.name: Rustic Pathways - Great Wall to Li River (China)
programs.description: A four-city, no-service-hours cultural/historical program: walking the Mutianyu Great Wall, the Forbidden City and Temple of Heaven in Beijing, sculpting a miniature terracotta warrior with a Xi'an craftsman near the actual Terracotta Army, a four-hour Li River cruise through karst peaks to Yangshuo with village fieldwork, and the Bund and Yuyuan Garden in Shanghai. IMPORTANT: US passport holders DO need a Chinese visa for this program (applied for in person, ~2 months lead time) -- unlike almost every other Rustic program, which requires no visa for US citizens. WhatsApp does not work in mainland China; every student gets a China-enabled SIM card and Program Leaders use WeChat instead. Max 18 students.
programs.priceDisplay: $5,280 at checkout ($5,180 tuition + $100 enrollment fee) + airfare

flags.title: US citizens need a Chinese visa for this program
flags.body: Unlike almost every other Rustic Pathways program, US passport holders DO need a visa to travel on this program, since it flies home directly to the United States rather than continuing to a third country. The visa must be applied for in person at a Chinese Visa Application Service Center, and families should start the process about two months before departure.
flags.sourceCitation: China: Great Wall to Li River program page, How Do Visas, Phones and Transport Work in China? section

flags.title: WhatsApp does not work in mainland China
flags.body: Families expecting to communicate via WhatsApp should know it does not function on mainland Chinese networks. Every student is issued a China-enabled SIM card, and Program Leaders and the Country Director use WeChat instead for non-emergency communication.
flags.sourceCitation: China: Great Wall to Li River program page, Communication FAQ section

flags.title: This program carries no community-service component
flags.body: Unlike many other Rustic Pathways programs, this one has no community service component and carries no service hours. Families specifically seeking service-hour documentation should choose a different program.
flags.sourceCitation: China: Great Wall to Li River program page, Is This the Right Fit? section

dayToDay.notes: Students stay in hotels throughout the four-city route (Beijing, Xi'an, Guilin/Yangshuo, Shanghai) in gender-separated shared rooms, supervised around the clock by Rustic Pathways staff, across nine hotel nights total. Median staff ratio 4.37:1 org-wide (never exceeding 7:1), max 18 students. Every student is issued a China-enabled SIM card so calls and texts home work normally throughout, since WhatsApp does not function in mainland China (Program Leaders use WeChat instead). Program Leaders run a deliberate 'First Friend Method' on Day 1 to ensure every student forms at least one real connection within the first 48 hours.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: China: Great Wall to Li River program page, Accommodation, Communication, and Group & Logistics FAQ sections

programs.name: Rustic Pathways - Shenzhen & Singapore: Two Models of Innovation
programs.description: The single most expensive program in the entire Rustic Pathways portfolio researched ($13,680 tuition). A corporate/urban-planning comparative program: inside DJI, Huawei, BYD and the Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) in Shenzhen, then Singapore's City Gallery planning model, Gardens by the Bay, BLOCK71 startup hub, and the National University of Singapore. Because the itinerary continues from China onward to a third country (Singapore), US citizens travel visa-free under China's 240-hour transit rule entering/exiting at Shenzhen Bao'an -- a different (and easier) visa situation than the standalone China program above, worth noting since both touch mainland China. Max 15 students.
programs.priceDisplay: $13,780 at checkout ($13,680 tuition + $100 enrollment fee) + airfare

flags.title: US citizens travel visa-free via China's 240-hour transit rule
flags.body: Because this itinerary enters mainland China directly from the US and continues onward to Singapore (a third country), students travel under China's 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit policy, entering and exiting at Shenzhen Bao'an. This is a materially different, easier visa situation than Rustic's standalone China program (Great Wall to Li River), which does require a visa since it returns directly to the US. Singapore itself is visa-free for US passport holders, with a free online Arrival Card required within 3 days of arrival.
flags.sourceCitation: Shenzhen & Singapore: Two Models of Innovation program page, visa FAQ section

flags.title: WhatsApp does not work during the Shenzhen (mainland China) portion
flags.body: As with Rustic's other mainland China program, WhatsApp does not function during the Shenzhen leg of this trip. Every student is issued a China-enabled SIM card, and Program Leaders use WeChat during that portion; normal connectivity resumes once the group reaches Singapore.
flags.sourceCitation: Shenzhen & Singapore: Two Models of Innovation program page, Communication FAQ section

flags.title: This is the most expensive program in the portfolio researched
flags.body: At $13,680 tuition ($13,780 at checkout), this is the single highest-priced program across all 29 Rustic Pathways programs researched -- more than six times the price of the least expensive program in this batch.
flags.sourceCitation: Shenzhen & Singapore: Two Models of Innovation program page, pricing section

dayToDay.notes: Students stay in centrally located hotels in both Shenzhen and Singapore, in gender-separated rooms of 2-4 students, supervised around the clock by Rustic Pathways staff. Median staff ratio 4.37:1 org-wide (never exceeding 7:1), max 15 students. Every student is issued a China-enabled SIM card for the Shenzhen leg so calls and texts home work normally, since WhatsApp does not function in mainland China (Program Leaders use WeChat instead); this switches back to normal connectivity once the group reaches Singapore.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Shenzhen & Singapore: Two Models of Innovation program page, Communication and Group & Logistics FAQ sections

programs.name: Rustic Pathways - Spanish Language Immersion (Turrialba, Costa Rica)
programs.description: The only one of Rustic's 4 Costa Rica programs built around living with a host family and studying Spanish every morning: 40 hours of ability-grouped Spanish instruction (open to complete beginners), 2 students per host household on full board, two full unscheduled Saturdays that belong entirely to the host family, and a whitewater rafting day on the Pacuare River. Max 16 students. Program Leaders live locally in Turrialba for the full two weeks rather than staying with the group.
programs.creditDisplay: 40 hours of Spanish instruction; course completion diploma (not a standardized proficiency certificate)
programs.priceDisplay: $4,595 at checkout ($4,495 tuition + $100 enrollment fee) + airfare

dayToDay.notes: Students live with a Costa Rican host family in Turrialba, two Rustic Pathways students per household (or three on request), on full board, for two weeks -- sleeping at the host family's house rather than with the group. Program Leaders are based locally in Turrialba for the full two weeks, see every student at the Spanish school each weekday, and are reachable at any hour, though they do not live in the host home itself. On the first and last nights, when the group is together in a San Jose hotel, students room with same-gender peers with staff in adjacent rooms. Both Sundays and one Saturday belong entirely to the host family with no Rustic Pathways programming. Max 16 students, placed two per household.

programs.name: Rustic Pathways - Spanish Language Immersion (Siguenza, Spain)
programs.description: Rustic's only Spain program that stays in one small town (Siguenza, a ~4,000-person medieval cathedral town in Castilla-La Mancha) with a two-week homestay: 42 hours of Spanish instruction customized to each student's home-school curriculum, workshops on Castilian music, Spanish painters, Don Quixote, and astronomy under a Starlight-certified dark sky, plus day trips to Madrid, Toledo, and Segovia. Two full unscheduled Saturdays belong to the host family. An alternative group-house option (El Albergue) exists for students not ready for a homestay. Max 20 students. Notably departs the US on a Saturday rather than Rustic's usual Wednesday pattern, because the partner school runs Sunday-to-Sunday.
programs.datesDisplay: June 19-July 4, 2027 (single session; departs Saturday, not the usual Wednesday)

This program instead departs Saturday, June 19, 2027 and returns Sunday, July 4, 2027, because its partner school (Segontiae Hispanic Studies) runs its course Sunday-to-Sunday. dayToDay.notes: Accommodation shifts across three settings. 5 nights in simple hotels with beds and bathrooms in San José and on the Caribbean coast; 6 nights in a rustic house in Turrialba near the local community, working and living alongside host families (a shared-house, host-family-adjacent arrangement rather than a traditional one-family homestay); and 2 nights at riverside campsites on raised jungle platform tents in the rainforest. Teens share tents or rooms based on gender and comfort, with leaders close by; flush toilets and short daily showers are available throughout. Everyone helps set up tents, clean shared spaces, and pack up gear. No staff ratio stated; given this serves grades 6-8, families should expect age-appropriate guidance though specific supervision detail beyond the general description is not provided.

programs.name: ActionQuest - Nova (British Virgin Islands)
programs.description: Condensed 10-day intro sailing and scuba voyage, shortest and lowest-priced AQ program. No experience necessary. IYT Try Sailing + PADI Discover Scuba or 2 sport dives. 12 students & 3 staff per vessel. Sails alongside wider fleet.

dayToDay.notes: Students live aboard a 45-50 ft monohull or catamaran full-time for the duration of the voyage, with 12 students and 3 staff per vessel (Skipper, first mate, and typically a third staff member such as a SCUBA instructor, medic, or marine biologist). Staff live aboard with students throughout. Each vessel has 5 cabins plus a large salon that converts to a 6th cabin, and 4 full bathrooms (heads); many students choose to sleep on deck under the stars in hammocks on clear nights. A rotating 'Job Wheel' assigns each student a different daily role (Skipper, Mate, Navigator, Engineer, Head Chef, plus support roles). Students prepare all meals themselves with staff help, using packaged/canned goods imported from the US plus fresh produce picked up locally roughly every 4 days; vegetarian, vegan, and common allergy accommodations are available with advance notice. Nova sails alongside the wider ActionQuest fleet (6-8 vessels) as a 'flotilla,' meeting the larger group at signature moments like beach BBQs. This day-to-day structure (staffing ratio, Job Wheel, Forum discussions, food policy, flotilla sailing) is standard across the ActionQuest British Virgin Islands fleet, not unique to Nova.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ActionQuest Nova program page, Accommodations, Food, and Group Living FAQ sections (org-wide fleet policy)

dayToDay.notes: Unlike the BVI live-aboard fleet, this program is a mixed land-and-sea itinerary in Australia: students stay in a mix of shore-based accommodations and time aboard a yacht sailing the Whitsunday Islands, with a group size of roughly 10-14 students and 2 staff (smaller than the typical BVI vessel of 12 students/3 staff). Includes hands-on community service work with the Daintree Observatory rainforest replanting project. dayToDay.notes: Lives aboard a 50-ft monohull or 46-ft catamaran with a smaller-than-typical group: 10 students and 2 staff per vessel, sailing in a small flotilla of just 1-2 vessels (versus the main BVI fleet's 6-8 vessels) for most of the voyage, though it begins and ends alongside the larger BVI fleet. programs.name: High Mountain Institute - Summer Term
programs.description: 4-week residential program in Leadville, Colorado, combining cabin-based campus life with two 10-day backpacking expeditions (8-10 students per group). Campus time includes a writing workshop or ecology research track (final essay or research project), plus rock climbing and Arkansas River whitewater rafting — not a backpacking-only trip. No previous outdoor experience required. Flexibility offered for students whose school year end date conflicts with the program start.

dayToDay.notes: Students split their 4 weeks between two settings. On campus in Leadville, Colorado, they live in cabins as part of a residential community, participating in writing workshops or ecology research, plus rock climbing at nearby crags and whitewater rafting on the Arkansas River. During the two 10-day backpacking expeditions, students travel in small expedition groups of 8-10 students, led by experienced HMI wilderness instructors who teach technical and wilderness travel skills; each group forms a tight-knit community over the course of the trip, and all students get the chance to take on leadership roles. The page does not detail a specific staff-to-student ratio for either the campus or expedition portions, nor describe cabin room-sharing arrangements or bathroom/shower facilities in the level of detail seen on some other providers' pages.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: High Mountain Institute Summer Term program page, main description and Why HMI Summer Term stats sections

programs.name: Where There Be Dragons - Bolivia: Spanish Language Immersion in the Andes
programs.description: 4-week Spanish immersion and trekking program through Bolivia, run in a small group of 12 students and 3 instructors. Begins with orientation and workshops in Candelaria near Sucre, then a 4-day trek through the Cordillera de los Frailes (ancient crater, cave drawings, dinosaur footprints, Quechua weaving communities) and a visit to an active mine in Potosi with the child-labor union Connatsop. Students then complete a 1-2 week homestay with a Quechua farming family in Tiquipaya near Cochabamba, receiving 30+ hours of daily Spanish instruction and pursuing an Independent Study Project (options include weaving, Andean music, traditional agriculture, Bolivian cooking, medicinal plants). The program closes with a student-led Expedition Phase: a 5-day trek descending from the high Andes (Cordillera Real, following an ancient Incan trail) into the Amazon cloud forest, ending at an eco-lodge in Coroico in the Yungas region. Approximately 10 hours of community-led service credit are earned. Program components are each rated Low/Medium/High on the page: Language Study, Social & Environmental Justice, Rugged Travel, Homestay, Independent Study Project, Religious & Spiritual Traditions, Trekking, and Learning Service.
programs.datesDisplay: June 28 - July 25, 2027 (single session; shown as Open availability)
programs.locationDisplay: Cochabamba, Sucre, Potosi, La Paz, Yungas/Coroico
programs.creditDisplay: Optional college credit (1-2 courses: COLS 191, CTE 191, CTE 292, SPAN 101/102/201); additional fee; 529 plan funds may apply

flags.title: This program involves extended high-altitude trekking, including a 5-day self-led descent
flags.body: Students trek through the Cordillera de los Frailes and Cordillera Real, both high-altitude Andean ranges, including a student-led 5-day trek during the program's 'Expedition Phase' where the group takes on increased responsibility for planning and logistics. Families should confirm their student's fitness level and any altitude-related health considerations directly with the provider, especially given the program also begins at El Alto International Airport, one of the highest-elevation international airports in the world.
flags.sourceCitation: Where There Be Dragons Bolivia program page, Program Description and Itinerary Example sections

This is more candidly disclosed than similar intensity notes on some other providers' pages, and families should take it as a genuine expectation-setter rather than boilerplate.

dayToDay.notes: Students travel in a single small group of 12 students and 3 instructors for the full 4 weeks, so this ratio (roughly 4:1) holds throughout every phase of the program rather than varying by activity. Accommodation type shifts by week: several nights in a workshop/orientation setting in Candelaria near Sucre; homestays with a Quechua farming family in Tiquipaya (near Cochabamba) for 1-2 weeks with few amenities described as part of the program's 'Rugged Travel' component; multi-day backcountry camping during both the Cordillera de los Frailes trek (week 2, 4 days) and the student-led Expedition Phase trek (week 4, 5 days, descending from the high Andes into cloud forest); and a final stay at an eco-lodge in Coroico. The program explicitly rates 'Rugged Travel' as a defining component, describing homestays with few amenities, extensive high-altitude walking, and lengthy public transportation travel. In week 4, students take on increased ownership over trip planning and logistics as part of the 'Expedition Phase,' a deliberate hand-off of responsibility rather than staff running the entire itinerary throughout.

Moves through an orientation stay in Sukhothai, a 3-day stay at a Buddhist monastery for a meditation retreat, a 5-day homestay with Karen community families in Huai Hin Lad Nai, a stay at Earth Home (a sustainable-living center), and a final student-led 2-day expedition phase in Chiang Rai (with instructor oversight) before closing in the mountains of Chiang Dao. No specific staff-to-student ratio beyond the 12:3 group size is stated.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Where There Be Dragons program page, Group Size and Program Components/Itinerary Example sections

programs.name: Where There Be Dragons - Morocco: Crossroads of Culture
programs.description: Begins with Arabic language orientation in the Middle Atlas Mountains, a 4-5 day semi-urban homestay in the Berber town of Azrou (language lessons, Independent Study Project planning), the UNESCO-listed medina of Fez (car-free old city, historic tanneries), and closes with a multi-day trek in the High Atlas Mountains through remote villages and nomadic communities (camping included). 12 students, 3 instructors.
programs.locationDisplay: Middle Atlas Mountains, Azrou, Fez, High Atlas Mountains
programs.creditDisplay: No college credit option mentioned on this page

flags.title: No college credit option is offered on this program
flags.body: Unlike several other WTBD summer programs researched, this page has no Optional College Credit section.
flags.sourceCitation: Absence of an Optional College Credit section on the program page

dayToDay.notes: 12 students and 3 instructors. Begins with an orientation stay in a small Middle Atlas Mountains town, then a 4-5 day semi-urban homestay in Azrou with Berber (Amazigh) families, city exploration in Fez (staying near the medina), and a closing multi-day trek with camping in the High Atlas Mountains through remote villages and nomadic communities. No specific staff-to-student ratio beyond the 12:3 group size is stated.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Where There Be Dragons program page, Group Size and Program Components/Itinerary Example sections

programs.name: Where There Be Dragons - Senegal: Youth Leadership, Arts, & Culture
programs.description: Centers on connecting with young Senegalese artists and activists: environmental activism and sea-turtle/coastline protection work near St. Louis, a stop in the holy city of Touba (one of the largest mosques in West Africa), a multi-day homestay in Thies with mentored arts study (drumming, dance, visual arts) and youth-activist guest speakers, a day trip to Dakar including the Island of Goree (Atlantic slave trade history) and the Museum of Black Civilization, and a closing Transference Phase on the cliffside beaches of Toubab Dialaw. 12 students, 3 instructors.
programs.locationDisplay: St. Louis, Touba, Thies, Dakar, Toubab Dialaw
programs.creditDisplay: No college credit option mentioned on this page

flags.title: The itinerary includes a visit to the Island of Goree and Atlantic slave trade history
flags.body: As part of the Dakar day trip, students visit the Island of Goree, a site associated with the history of the Atlantic slave trade, and the Museum of Black Civilization. This is substantive historical content; families should be aware this isn't a purely recreational cultural program.
flags.sourceCitation: Program page, Days 7-12 itinerary section

dayToDay.notes: 12 students and 3 instructors. Days spent in a seaside community inside a national park near St. Louis (day-stays with local families for meals), then a stop in Touba, and a multi-day homestay in Thies with local families for the bulk of the program, including a day trip to Dakar. Closes on the cliffside beaches of Toubab Dialaw for a group Transference Phase. No specific staff-to-student ratio beyond the 12:3 group size is stated.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Where There Be Dragons program page, Group Size and Program Components/Itinerary Example sections

programs.name: Camp Laurel - Full Season
programs.description: Traditional, full-season (7-week) coed sleepaway camp on Echo Lake in the Belgrade Lakes region of Maine, ACA accredited. Most activities single-gender within a coed camp. Six campuses (3 boys, 3 girls) subdivided by grade. Younger campers follow a structured schedule; older campers build individualized schedules with more choice. In-camp leagues plus intercamp competition, open participation. Non-denominational. 3:1+ camper-to-staff ratio.
programs.datesDisplay: June 26 - August 11, 2027 (single full-season session; Visiting Day July 24)
programs.locationDisplay: Belgrade Lakes region (Readfield / Kents Hill), Maine
programs.priceDisplay: $18,500 tuition, plus optional add-ons: $600 trip day/personal expenses, $1,500-$2,500 equestrian (3 or 5 days/week), $700-$975 extended trip fee (grades 7-9), transportation varies by location

flags.title: Several optional add-on fees can meaningfully increase the total cost
flags.body: Trip day ($600), equestrian ($1,500-$2,500), extended trip fee ($700-$975 for grades 7-9), and transportation (varies) are all separate from the $18,500 base tuition.
flags.sourceCitation: Camp Laurel Dates & Fees page

flags.title: The camp is coed overall, but most activities are single-gender
flags.body: All athletics are grouped by gender and ability within age group, despite the camp being coed overall.
flags.sourceCitation: Camp Laurel program/FAQ pages on campus structure and athletics grouping

dayToDay.notes: Six campuses (3 boys, 3 girls), subdivided into cabin groups by grade. Wake-up 7:45am (older campuses) or 8:10am (younger); bedtime 8:30pm-11:00pm scaling with age. Typical day: wake-up/breakfast, morning 'Cove' gathering, cabin clean-up, 3 morning activities, buffet lunch, rest hour, 2 afternoon activities, all-camp 6th period (free choice for older campers, shower/down-time for younger), dinner, evening Cove, evening cabin program, bedtime. Two seatings for breakfast/dinner; whole camp eats lunch together. 3:1+ camper-to-staff ratio; counselors mostly college students/teachers, most over 20. Younger campers have required activities (swim/tennis lessons, team sports); older campers build individualized schedules and can specialize. All cabins have electricity and overnight night-lights.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Camp Laurel FAQ page, multiple Q&A entries on daily schedule, campus structure, staff ratio, and wake-up/bedtime times

programs.name: Envision (NYLF) - Medicine & Health Care
programs.description: An 8-day pre-college medical program (part of the National Youth Leadership Forum series, acquired by Envision in 2007) combining hands-on clinical-skills rotations (suturing, blood pressure, phlebotomy, neuro exams), two full simulation days (a Disaster Triage simulation and an Outdoor Emergency Medicine / wilderness-medicine simulation originally developed with Stanford School of Medicine faculty), a tour of a medical school or simulation center, guest speaker panels with practicing clinicians, and a final medical case-study presentation. Runs at six university campuses in 2027 with residential-only pricing/dates confirmed; a commuter option exists (on-campus lunches included, no room & board) but 2027 commuter pricing was not shown on this page. Optional add-ons include a private airport shuttle (extra fee) and a partnership offering with Polygence (independent research mentorship).
programs.creditDisplay: 1-2 college credits (residential: 2; commuter: 1) from George Mason University, as a non-degree high school guest student
programs.priceDisplay: $4,499.00 (residential; commuter pricing not shown for 2027 on this page)

flags.title: A documented complaint alleges college credit is not delivered in time to use on college applications
flags.body: This program advertises college credit (1-2 credits from George Mason University, as a non-degree high school guest student) as a core selling point, included in tuition. A 2-star Trustpilot review (July 2025) describes this as feeling like a "bait and switch": the reviewer states they paid roughly $5,000 expecting the credit to strengthen a college application, but the credit was not delivered in time for that purpose, and when they contacted Envision, they were told responsibility for the credit and its timing rests with George Mason University rather than with Envision, the company the family actually contracted with. This is a single review rather than a confirmed pattern, but it directly concerns the exact credit-granting mechanism this program uses, so families relying on the credit for a specific application deadline should confirm the actual transcript delivery timeline directly with Envision and George Mason University before enrolling, rather than assuming the credit will post before college application deadlines.
flags.sourceCitation: Trustpilot review of envisionexperience.com (French-language Trustpilot page, dated July 14, 2025, rated 2 out of 5 stars, titled "Warning: You wont get your college credit in time")

flags.title: Several 2027 sessions are marked 'Save My Spot' rather than directly bookable
flags.body: The Rice, Yale, and University of Michigan sessions all display confirmed 2027 dates and prices but are labeled 'Save my spot for 2027' rather than offering a direct 'Enroll Now' path like the Berkeley, UCLA, and Emory sessions. This likely means these sessions are not yet fully open for enrollment even though pricing and dates are published. Families interested in these specific campuses should confirm current enrollment status directly.
flags.sourceCitation: Envision NYLF Medicine & Health Care program page, Dates & Locations section

flags.title: College credit is earned as a 'non-degree guest' student, not enrolled coursework
flags.body: The credit is explicitly described as earned "as a non-degree high school guest" at George Mason University. Families should confirm with their target colleges how this specific credit type transfers or is weighted in admissions review, since non-degree guest credit may be treated differently than credit from a student's own enrolled coursework.
flags.sourceCitation: Envision NYLF Medicine & Health Care program page, College Credit section

flags.title: 2027 commuter pricing was not shown on this page

Families interested in the commuter track should confirm current pricing directly.
flags.sourceCitation: Envision NYLF Medicine & Health Care program page, What does the price include? and Dates & Locations sections

Families should not assume university-level oversight, faculty employment, or institutional endorsement simply because the program is held on a college campus.

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live in dorms on the host university campus for the full 8 days, with an Advisor and classroom group assigned on Day 1 alongside icebreaker activities. Days follow a consistent structure: morning career-exploration or workshop sessions, afternoon hands-on clinical-skills rotations or simulations (suturing, blood pressure, phlebotomy, disaster triage, wilderness/outdoor emergency medicine), and organized evening 'Team Time' social activities (ice cream social, scavenger hunt, trivia night, talent show). One day includes a site visit to a medical school or simulation center, with lunch or dinner off campus. Commuter students attend the same daytime programming (on-campus lunches included) but do not stay overnight or participate in evening Team Time activities. The page does not state a specific staff-to-student ratio beyond describing an 'Advisor' assigned to each classroom group. Health and safety oversight is described at the organizational level: Envision partners with Exlog (an international security firm) and monitors State Department and CDC guidance, with local support described as available 24/7.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Envision NYLF Medicine & Health Care program page, Sample Itinerary and Health & Safety sections

See flags file for the standing complaint about George Mason credit delivery timing, which applies to this program.
programs.creditDisplay: 1-2 college credits from George Mason University, as a non-degree high school guest student

flags.title: A documented complaint alleges college credit is not delivered in time to use on college applications
flags.body: This program advertises college credit from George Mason University (as a non-degree high school guest student) as a core selling point, included in tuition. A 2-star Trustpilot review (July 2025) describes this as feeling like a "bait and switch": the reviewer paid roughly $5,000 expecting the credit to strengthen a college application, but the credit was not delivered in time for that purpose, and Envision reportedly redirected responsibility to George Mason University rather than the company the family contracted with. This is a single review rather than a confirmed pattern, but it concerns the exact credit-granting mechanism this program uses. Families relying on the credit for a specific application deadline should confirm the actual transcript delivery timeline directly with Envision and George Mason University before enrolling.
flags.sourceCitation: Trustpilot review of envisionexperience.com (French-language Trustpilot page, dated July 14, 2025, rated 2 out of 5 stars, titled "Warning: You wont get your college credit in time")

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live in dorms on the host university campus, structured around morning career-exploration sessions, afternoon hands-on workshops/simulations, and organized evening social activities. programs.name: Envision - Veterinary Academy: Horse & Large Animal Medicine (New York)
programs.description: Works at Pine Bush Equine Services & Veterinary Hospital and local equine rescue facilities, earning up to 40 veterinary hours toward vet school applications, covering large animal medicine (one of vet schools' six key required experience categories) including a working horse breeding facility visit. Housed at SUNY New Paltz. Run in partnership with Loop Abroad, described as the leading pre-veterinary travel program in the nation. 10:1 student-to-veterinarian ratio, maximum 30 students.
programs.datesDisplay: July 11-17, 2027 (Pine Bush Equine Services, SUNY New Paltz housing)

flags.title: Program involves direct hands-on work with rescued and rehabilitation horses
flags.body: Students perform physical exams, injections, and suturing practice on live animals (including rescued horses, donkeys, cows, goats, sheep, and chickens) under veterinary supervision. Families should discuss comfort with direct animal handling and any allergy considerations directly with the provider.
flags.sourceCitation: Program page, Why This Program Changes Everything section

dayToDay.notes: Days follow a consistent structure: morning veterinary lectures and field classes, afternoon animal-care rotations (food preparation, enclosure maintenance, animal enrichment) alternating with hands-on veterinary lab activities (suturing, bandaging, parasitology, radiograph interpretation, blood cytology), and evening social 'Team Time' activities. Students work toward a student-led 'Keeper Talk' presentation to real visitors by the end of the week. Run in partnership with Loop Abroad; veterinarians and senior staff are industry professionals (bachelor's degree or above), and support staff are often college students in veterinary school or education, many of them Loop Abroad program alumni. Envision staff cannot administer any medication, including over-the-counter medication -- students self-manage medication using a completed Medication Administration Form. Roommates are assigned by age unless a same-gender, same-session roommate request is submitted online at least 3 weeks before the session; a roommate is not guaranteed and some students may be placed in single rooms. Vegetarian meals are available everywhere; other dietary needs (vegan, kosher, halal, gluten-free, allergies) are handled as individual requests through the Office of Admissions. An onsite staff member is available 24 hours a day with a direct cell number provided to students. 10:1 student-to-veterinarian ratio, maximum 30 students. Students stay at SUNY New Paltz with daily transfers to Pine Bush Equine Services.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Envision Veterinary Academy: Horse & Large Animal Medicine (New York) program page, Sample Itinerary and FAQ sections

programs.description: Held at American University; includes a Smithsonian National Zoo visit, a working farm visit, and a brief D.C. monuments bus tour. dayToDay.notes: Held at American University with a mix of on-site labs (suturing, dissection, microscope work, first aid) and field trips to a local zoo and a farm, plus a brief D.C. monuments bus tour. programs.name: Envision (Oxbridge Academic Programs) - The Oxford Tradition
programs.description: A separate Envision subsidiary brand (Oxbridge Academic Programs, operating for 40+ years, distinct from the NYLF/George Mason credit model). Students choose one course per 2-week session from ~20 subjects (Medicine, Law, International Relations, Business, Engineering, Psychology, and more) taught by Oxford/Cambridge-affiliated faculty including Rhodes and Fulbright Scholars, living at historic Pembroke College (founded 1624). Class sizes capped at 15. Strict nightly curfew (check-in by 9-10pm, lights out 11pm) and a zero-tolerance alcohol/drug policy with immediate expulsion for violations.
programs.creditDisplay: No transferable university credit; students receive comprehensive grade reports (syllabus + instructor-noted contributions) intended for use in college applications

flags.title: No transferable college credit is awarded, only grade reports
flags.body: Unlike Envision's NYLF programs (which include George Mason University credit), this Oxbridge Academic Programs offering explicitly does not award transferable university credit -- students instead receive comprehensive grade reports intended for use in college applications. This is a meaningfully different value proposition; families should not assume the standing NYLF college-credit complaint applies here.
flags.sourceCitation: Program page FAQ, 'Do I Get a Certificate or University Credit After Completing the Program?'

flags.title: Strict nightly curfew and zero-tolerance alcohol/drug policy with immediate expulsion
flags.body: Students must check in twice nightly with a Dean and are not permitted to leave campus after check-in; any alcohol or drug violation results in immediate expulsion with no stated appeal process described on the page.
flags.sourceCitation: Program page FAQ, security-related questions

dayToDay.notes: A typical day begins with breakfast in the residence dining hall, followed by a morning class (sometimes held off-site at a museum, lab, or historic landmark). Students purchase their own lunch during a midday break, then have an afternoon Major or Minor class/workshop. Evenings include a full, though optional, calendar of social/cultural activities (sports, concerts, tours, talent shows) before a group dinner and a nightly curfew. Security: students must check in at dinner and again between 9:00-10:00pm with an assigned Dean; lights out is 11:00pm; once checked in, students are not permitted to leave campus. College entrances are supervised round-the-clock by College Porters, Campus Security, and Envision/Oxbridge staff, with CCTV coverage. Some staff (Program Director, Deans, Program Assistants, Activities Directors, Medical Officer) live in the residences alongside students for round-the-clock supervision, though a specific staff-to-student ratio is not given (described as varying by program location and size). A strict zero-tolerance policy against alcohol and drugs applies, with immediate expulsion for any violation. Students are housed in gender-separated hallways or floors. A qualified Medical Officer is present at every venue. Housed at Pembroke College, Oxford.

flags.title: Scuba diving involves real depth limits that scale by age and certification
flags.body: Maximum depth is 60ft for standard certified divers and up to 80-90ft for the most advanced students. Divers aged 11 are capped at 40ft and must dive with a PADI professional or certified diver; ages 12-14 may go to 70ft only with additional Junior Advanced Open Water training. Families should weigh their child's comfort and readiness for open-water diving at these depths, and confirm their child's actual certification status meets the Open Water (or equivalent) prerequisite before enrolling.

dayToDay.notes: Students must hold PADI Open Water certification or equivalent to enroll. Diving is conducted from a dedicated fleet of custom Newton dive boats (separate from the sailing yachts, to keep gear and compressors off the sailboats), operated by Sail Caribbean Divers, a PADI 5-Star Instructor Development Dive Center with three land-based locations in the BVI. Dive staff-to-student ratio is 5:1. Maximum dive depth is 60ft for standard certified divers and up to 80-90ft for the most advanced students; divers aged 11 are capped at 40ft and must dive with a PADI professional or certified diver; ages 12-14 with additional Junior Advanced Open Water training may go to 70ft. Equipment is rinsed in freshwater after every dive per PADI-recommended practice. Dive staff regularly drill with VISAR (the BVI's volunteer marine search and rescue organization) and have assisted with real rescues.
