programs.name: Northwaters & Langskib - Northwaters All Gender (Coed)
programs.description: An all-gender wilderness canoe-tripping program for ages 13-17, run by Northwaters & Langskib (NWL) in the Temagami region of Ontario. After a few days at base camp building backcountry skills (portaging, packing a Duluth bag and wannigan, tent setup, paddling) and establishing group norms (honesty, acceptance, trust, patience, humour) with the full cohort, participants split into sections of 6-12 participants led by 2-3 staff for a roughly 20-day canoe trip, with routes ranging from local lake/stream excursions to more challenging whitewater river expeditions depending on the section's skill and experience level. All sections return to base camp on the same day for a shared celebration, feast, and gear de-outfitting, followed by a joint event with the brother program Langskib (for boys/young men) when their cohort arrives by Voyageur canoe. Tuition covers all activities, guides, food, river-trip shuttles, reprovisioning, and group gear.
programs.locationDisplay: Temagami, Ontario, Canada (island base camp on a lake, with canoe routes extending across the region)
programs.priceDisplay: $5,850 USD tuition, plus Canadian sales tax (calculated separately) and optional bus travel from Toronto or Ottawa

flags.title: A second 2027 session may exist but is not listed in the Coed program's own table
flags.body: The Dates & Rates page's Summer 2027 Calendar footnote explicitly references "Northwaters/Langskib 2nd Sessions" beginning July 22 and ending August 14, 2027 -- the same window as Langskib's confirmed second session. However, the Northwaters Coed table itself lists only the single June 26-July 19 session (plus the by-invitation Leadership Program variant). This could mean Coed genuinely runs only one general-enrollment session in 2027 while Langskib runs two, or it could be an editing gap on the page. Families interested in a July/August timeframe should confirm directly with the provider whether a second Coed session is available before assuming none exists.
flags.sourceCitation: Northwaters Dates & Rates page: comparison between the Summer 2027 Calendar section and the Northwaters Coed program table

dayToDay.notes: The program begins with a full-group gathering at base camp (an island on a lake in Temagami) where staff and all participants discuss the community they're forming and agree on shared values (honesty, acceptance, trust, patience, humour). The first few days are spent building backcountry travel skills with staff and more experienced participants: portaging, packing a Duluth bag and wannigan, setting up a tent, and paddling technique. Once the group is acquainted, participants are divided into 'sections' of 6-12 participants led by 2-3 staff, formed according to individual needs, skill level, and group dynamics -- these sections then embark on their own canoe-tripping route, ranging from local lake/stream excursions near base camp to more challenging whitewater river expeditions, depending on the section's experience and skill. Leaders draw on training and experience to guide each group through the trip, building trust, communication, and community as the section sets goals, solves problems together, and makes decisions collectively. All sections return to base camp on the same day, arriving within minutes of each other to a staff-and-director welcome on the docks, followed by a shared feast and storytelling in the dining hall. The next day is spent re-integrating into the larger camp community: de-outfitting canoe trip gear, doing 'giveaways,' and a ceremony honoring each participant's accomplishments and contributions. The following day, participants from the brother program Langskib (for boys/young men) arrive by Voyageur canoe for a joint barbecue and celebration, where sections from both programs share stories from the trail.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Northwaters All Gender (Coed) program page (Arriving at Base Camp, The 20-Day Canoe Trip, and Returning Home sections)

programs.name: World Class Programs - Spain (Seville)
programs.description: A 2-week language-immersion and cultural-studies program based in Seville, with weekend day trips to Madrid, Cordoba, and Gibraltar. Major class options: Spanish History, Fine Art & Drawing, Spanish Language (Beginner or Advanced/Immersion). Minor options: Philosophy, Photography, Spanish Cuisine. Includes a Traditional (Flamenco) Dance workshop. Students live in staff-controlled apartments/hotels (not homestays), typically 2-4 students per bedroom, with staff housed separately in the same building. A dedicated World Class Programs Security Officer, on-call 24/7, is provided when a program is large enough to warrant one (not guaranteed on smaller programs). Academic structure: each student picks a major (meets every weekday morning) and a minor/elective (meets three afternoons a week: Monday, Wednesday, Friday), plus weekend day-trips to other cities in the region. Housing here is specifically described as 2-3 bedroom apartments with 2 students sharing each bedroom, slightly more specific than the 2-4-per-bedroom figure given on the other program pages.

dayToDay.notes: Students live in upscale student apartments in central Seville, controlled by World Class Programs and shared only with other World Class students (no host families). Apartments have living rooms, kitchens, bathrooms, and 2-3 bedrooms, each shared by two students; staff are housed in a separate apartment down the hall from students. A dedicated Security Officer stays in the building, on-call to students 24/7. Weekday structure: major class (Spanish History, Fine Art & Drawing, or Spanish Language at Beginner or Advanced/Immersion level) meets every weekday morning; minor/elective class meets three afternoons a week (Monday, Wednesday, Friday). On non-minor-class afternoons, students join a group activity. Weekends are used for day trips to other Spanish cities (Madrid, Cordoba, Gibraltar). Free time is available for the city's cafe scene and shopping districts "within safety guidelines."

programs.name: World Class Programs - Greece & Italy: Western Civilization
programs.description: A 3-week classical-history and archaeology program spanning the Greek Isles and southern Italy, with planned visits (subject to change year to year) to Santorini, Mykonos, Crete, the Ruins of Ephesus, the Amalfi Coast/Positano, and Pompeii. Major class options: Classical History & Archaeology, Fine Art & Drawing, Western Religion & Traditions. Minor options: Western Philosophy, Digital Photography, Mediterranean Cuisine. Students live in staff-controlled apartments/hotels (not homestays), typically 2-4 students per bedroom, with staff housed separately in the same building. A dedicated World Class Programs Security Officer, on-call 24/7, is provided when a program is large enough to warrant one (not guaranteed on smaller programs). Academic structure: each student picks a major (meets every weekday morning) and a minor/elective (meets three afternoons a week: Monday, Wednesday, Friday), plus weekend day-trips to other cities in the region. This is Worldwide Class's most expensive program at $7,995 (matching Greece to the top price tier alongside the 3-week Japan option) and the only one combining two countries in a single program.
